ISTJ.strength: Lean into your reliability. When a team is scattered or a plan is vague, you're the one who can turn it into something concrete and dependable, don't undersell how rare that is.
ISTJ.weakness: Watch for treating "the way we've always done it" as the same thing as "the right way." Build in a regular, deliberate check for whether the process still fits the situation, not just whether it's being followed.

ISFJ.strength: Lean into your attentiveness. You notice what people actually need before they ask, use that instinct deliberately instead of just reacting to it.
ISFJ.weakness: Watch for saying yes to keep the peace when you actually disagree. Practice naming a real objection early, before it turns into quiet resentment.

INFJ.strength: Lean into your ability to see the pattern behind a situation. Say it out loud earlier, your insight helps the room more before a decision is made than after.
INFJ.weakness: Watch for going from fully engaged to completely checked out with no warning. Build in a habit of naming when you're withdrawing, rather than just disappearing.

INTJ.strength: Lean into your long-range thinking. When a team is stuck reacting to the moment, you're the one who can name where this is actually headed.
INTJ.weakness: Watch for treating disagreement as inefficiency. Slow down enough to hear out a different approach fully before deciding it's wrong.

ISTP.strength: Lean into your calm under pressure. When something breaks and everyone else is panicking, you're the one who can actually fix it.
ISTP.weakness: Watch for going quiet instead of flagging that you're stuck. A quick heads-up costs you nothing and saves everyone else from guessing.

ISFP.strength: Lean into your quiet conviction. When you actually hold your ground on something, people notice, use that more deliberately, not just when you're pushed.
ISFP.weakness: Watch for letting a disagreement go unspoken because raising it feels like conflict. A perspective withheld helps no one, including you.

INFP.strength: Lean into your sense of what actually matters. You see potential in people and ideas before anyone else does, say so before the moment passes.
INFP.weakness: Watch for finishing the exciting 80 percent and quietly abandoning the last 20. Build a deliberate habit around closing things out, not just starting them.

INTP.strength: Lean into your depth. When a problem needs someone to actually understand it, not just move fast on it, that's you, don't rush past that value.
INTP.weakness: Watch for refining a conclusion long after it was already good enough. Set yourself a deliberate point to stop and share, even if it's not fully polished.

ESTP.strength: Lean into your comfort acting on incomplete information. When a team is stuck overanalyzing, you're the one who can actually move things forward.
ESTP.weakness: Watch for skipping the people who needed to be consulted because you were moving fast. A quick check-in costs less than the cleanup after.

ESFP.strength: Lean into your genuine warmth. You lift a room without even trying, that's a real skill, not just a personality trait, use it deliberately in tense moments.
ESFP.weakness: Watch for reading a flat reaction as personal failure. Not every room is about you, separate the outcome from your own worth before reacting.

ENFP.strength: Lean into your ability to spot a new possibility others miss. Say it even when it's half-formed, the room needs the spark more than the polish.
ENFP.weakness: Watch for chasing the next idea before the current one is actually finished. Pick one thing to see all the way through before starting something new.

ENTP.strength: Lean into your instinct to question assumptions. When a team is about to commit to something on autopilot, you're the one who actually stress-tests it.
ENTP.weakness: Watch for turning a useful debate into a battle you need to win. Notice when the relationship matters more than being right, and let it go.

ESTJ.strength: Lean into your ability to bring order to chaos. When a team needs clear structure and a real decision, you're the one who delivers it.
ESTJ.weakness: Watch for pushing harder for control exactly when the situation calls for flexibility. Pause before tightening your grip, and ask what the moment actually needs.

ESFJ.strength: Lean into your instinct to keep people connected and included. A team runs better because you notice who's being left out, keep doing that deliberately.
ESFJ.weakness: Watch for taking on more than your share to keep everyone happy. Practice naming what you're stretched thin on before it becomes resentment.

ENFJ.strength: Lean into your ability to genuinely bring out the best in people. When someone doubts themselves, you're often the reason they don't quit, keep doing that on purpose.
ENFJ.weakness: Watch for pouring into everyone else while your own reserves run empty. Protecting your own energy isn't selfish, it's what lets you keep showing up.

ENTJ.strength: Lean into your decisiveness. When a team is stuck circling a decision, you're the one who can actually call it and move.
ENTJ.weakness: Watch for pushing decisions through without bringing people along. A fast decision that no one buys into is often slower in the end.
